requirements.requirement: Rotate /var/log/inventory/app.log daily and retain seven compressed rotations.
requirements.summary: The installed policy specifies daily rotation, seven retained archives, and compression. Logrotate parsed those settings successfully, a forced behavioral test produced a valid gzip archive, and the policy, state, active timer, and archive remained intact after restart.

requirements.requirement: Allow the application to continue writing after rotation.
requirements.summary: A writer held the log open across an actual rotation. The active log retained the same inode and received the post-rotation record, while the pre-rotation data was present in the compressed archive. The resulting active and archived data also survived restart.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel, using software compatible with the platform.
requirements.summary: Before and after execution, the node remained CentOS Stream 10 on kernel 6.12.0-205.el10.x86_64. The implementation used the already-installed EL10 logrotate 3.22.0 package and existing system timer; package health remained clean.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The mandatory node-restart protocol is also complete: healthy pre-restart state and boot ID were captured, restart was acknowledged, the connection disruption was observed, the boot ID changed, and the system, timer, policy, active log, and compressed archive recovered. Fixed lifecycle boot identities independently corroborate the restart.
limitations: The evidence validates the seven-archive retention setting through logrotate's parser and one real compressed rotation; it does not exercise eight successive rotations to observe oldest-archive eviction.
Daily eligibility is directly shown by the parsed policy and active scheduler, but the short evidence window does not include a naturally timed next-day rotation.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Creating the logrotate policy was the required implementation (cmd-7a2e2a190cbc4af8); the bounded writer/forced-rotation test changed log contents and rotation state solely to establish final behavior (cmd-6494d5b9334d4b4d); and the scheduled reboot was required by the provider-wide restart protocol (cmd-d8a4f171fbd54943). Other commands were read-only observations. Post-execution snapshots show no failed services, damaged package state, new exposure, or abandoned temporary residue; socket and systemd-private path differences are normal consequences of the verified reboot.
